text.p: ZAGREB, May 26 (reuter) - Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuaracy.

- "We shall endure pressure with decisiveness and calm," said president Franjo Tudjman in an interview, responding to Western diplomats who demanded free return of Serb refugees to their homes accross Croatia.
- Social democrat Zdravko Tomac, liberal Vlado Gotovac and current president Tudjman are candidates at the next presidential elections in June.
- Foreign telecommunication companies see Croatia as an interesting market for mobile telephones, still relatively scarce by European standards.
- Stock Exchange: Two new brokerages founded by Austria's Creditanstaltbank (CAIB) and Bank Austria became full members of Zagreb's bourse last week.
- Drivers from the port of Split are among the heaviest drinkers in Croatia, police says after checking thousands of cars in their 'weekend actions'.
- Former German Foreign Minister Hans Dietrich Gescher becomes an honorary citizen on Osijek.
- High telephone bills and costly hotels worried foreign journalists who took part at Damatia Cup 97 promotional regata. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
